newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigerian shares bullish in moderate trade.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian shares bullish in moderate trade.

text.p: Rising stocks crowded out fallers in what dealers said was a moderately active Friday's trading on the Nigerian stock exchange.
The all-share index closed at 6,590.33 points from 6,910.30 on Thursday.
Speculative demand for oil, brewing and food shares dictated the pace, dealers said.
Unipetrol chalked up a 1.50 naira gain to 56.50 naira. Total closed 35 kobo higher at 56.55 naira.

Nigerian Breweries moved closer to its highest level this year as an 80 kobo appreciation lifted it to 19.30. It opened at 19.89 naira in January but went on free fall to 10.00 naira in October before rallying in November.
Guinness also rose 38 kobo to 8.08 naira on positive perception.
Nestle's good run continued, closing 70 kobo up at 47.70 naira. Union Dicon Salt too rose on strong demand to 43.40 naira, up 40 kobo.
Traders said West African Portland Cement Company advanced 1.50 naira to 44.50 naira on equally healthy demand.
Troubled conglomerates and manufacturing concerns fell further as more shares were poured into the market looking for buyers.

Lever Brothers and Cadbury were down 50 kobo each at 21.00 naira and 22.50 naira respectively. Guaranty Trust Bank slid 30 kobo to 12.00 naira and Union Bank was 20 kobo lower at 4.85 naira. Ashaka Cement ended 20 kobo lower at 17.20 naira.
CFAO fell 14 kobo to 2.76 naira on falling profits shown in third-quarter results.
Traders said the outlook for the conglomerates was still gloomy as investors were still dumping them.
